overview: Lean project on 12 wards in Hospitals A to D with a staggered start that follows the single Lean coach: Hospital A maps and starts standard work in January 2027, B in April, C in July and D in October. Each hospital keeps its own measurement source for the whole series, and the hospitals not yet started serve as concurrent controls.
population: Adult inpatients on the 12 participating medical and surgical wards; all catheterised patients, including those catheterised in emergency or theatres before transfer.
exposure: Standard work introduced at each hospital's start: nurse-driven removal protocol approved by that hospital's medical advisory committee, a daily catheter check at the morning huddle and a removal reminder (flowsheet in A to C, a huddle board prompt in D).
procedures: Each champion leads a two-day mapping event with the coach in the hospital's first month, then standard work starts. Hospitals A to C take catheter days from the flowsheet from January 2026, giving 12 to 21 baseline months. Hospital D starts twice-weekly point counts in November 2026 and keeps them for its whole series, so its source never switches (c5). Indication documentation is checked on 20 charts per ward per month; reinsertion within 72 hours and infections follow the regional surveillance definitions. Hospital D's ward-level data stay in the hospital until its information governance office agrees to sharing.

outcomes.name: Catheter days per 100 patient days
outcomes.measure: Monthly catheter days divided by patient days, per ward; flowsheet in A to C, point-count estimate in D
outcomes.timing: Monthly from each hospital's baseline to March 2028
outcomes.why: Responsive to removal practice (c1); measured consistently within each series.

outcomes.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections per 1,000 catheter days
outcomes.why: The harm patients care about; descriptive only (c2).

outcomes.name: Catheters without a documented indication
outcomes.measure: Proportion of 20 sampled catheterised patients per ward per month
outcomes.why: Tracks the handoff failure found in mapping (c3).

outcomes.name: Reinsertion within 72 hours of removal
outcomes.measure: Reinsertions divided by removals, reported by age group

biasMitigation: Staggered starts so that hospitals not yet started act as concurrent controls

Annotated charts for co-interventions and staffing changes

biasFlags.label: Secular trend
biasFlags.note: Staggered starts separate each start from regional trends.

biasFlags.label: Different measurement source in Hospital D
biasFlags.note: Analysed with a site-specific level; never pooled with a switch of source.

biasFlags.label: Surveillance intensity
biasFlags.note: More attention to catheters may find more infections.

Site-specific level for Hospital D instead of a second primary measure
parsimony.simplestPath: Monthly catheter days per ward with one start date per hospital.

feasibility: One coach for three months per hospital; about 3 staff hours a month for point counts in Hospital D; chart review limited to 20 charts per ward per month for indication documentation.
theoreticalFramework: Lean value stream mapping and standard work; SEIPS only to describe the work system at handoffs.
summary: Revised protocol: staggered starts that follow the coach, and Hospital D measured by point counts for its whole series.
